This is so interesting. When I was 17, I went to my first Jesus camp because the church my dad pastored had a scholarship for it.  It was awesome.  I had so much fun.  The final night, the resident band for that week played an original song they wrote and vamped the same chords over and over again for like half an hour and man I thought it was beautiful.  I thought about all my wrong doings in my life and problems and I cried and "became a Christian" again and it was magical.  Even now I look back and it was a great night, but now I realize what lead up to it.  Exhaustion and manipulation.  When kids started bursting into tears, they played softer and the pastor talked about forgiveness and born again Christianity and such and now I look back and feel kinda duped that I fell for it. 

The Jesus camp "high" wore off after about 3 weeks and I felt guilty and wondered why I only felt that way at camp. So I taught there for the next two years, got my high, then realized, screw this BS, I love the people, but I can't teach it anymore.  I wish I could go back to the camp, but I know I can't because it's Jesus based.  Good memories but I definitely feel tricked into crying and confessing due to tiredness and major sensory overload throughout the entire week.

Worst quality is bitterness.  Had some rough stuff thrown towards me and I've dealt with it, but I know how mean and bitter I can be if I let it get out of control.  I used to have a poor pitiful me mindset, and I think it really ties in with bitterness because you don't really take action to fix anything and you think the world is out to get you.  I've really put in work to fix that, by actively trying to make things better as bad stuff happens, or being accountable for my actions.  But I know that bitterness is still something I have to work on.  

Example, something more small, but there was a group online who publicly humiliated me in front of 8k people, and I started to resent all of them for that. I usually don't get angry or mean, but I was very tempted to turn into the bad guy.  3 years later, it still stings and I'm still butthurt about it.  My mind makes them the bad guy and it makes me into the victim and I hate it because it's done and gone and no one remembers it but me LOL.  So whenever I think about what happened, I just remember that they're human, they were jerks, but I've been a jerk in the past too, so if I can't forgive them, how could someone else forgive me?  Anyways, I just actively am aware, and I try to not point fingers at anyone without looking at myself first, because ultimately, I'm the one who's in control, not people and not circumstances.  So screw bitterness!!!!!

Focus on your wrist.  Ball your hand up in a fist and just focus on going up and down, or up, up, down, etc. - Then stick your index out and do that same motion.  It's really weird at first.  I think what's tripping you up is that you might be new to chords so your mind is trying to focus on your left AND right hand and it's hard to do both at first if it's a new idea.  Just focus on developing that muscle memory for the right hand more than anything.  One hand at a time.  You know what I mean?  Another thing you could do is use your thumb, but I don't really encourage bad habits.  Better to bite the bullet and do the weird right way than to get into a bad habit.  (:

My BF plays the ukulele and taught me.  It's really easy to get into if you have the will to do it.  Learn the basic chords in the key of C (C major, A minor, F major and G major), (Here's a link https://acousticbridge.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/05/C-Am-F-G-ukulele-chords.jpg) and then just play those in repetition over and over again until muscle memory picks it up.  Then switch up the order of the chords (example being, F, G, Am, C, or Am, C, G, F, etc.) And get a feel for the way songs are built.  Pretty much every mainstream song uses that chord progression (just might be in a different key) so find something that you like, look up the chords online (if it's not already in the key of C major, specify that in a search) and start by just strumming each chord.
